posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Silverleaf:

I think it's just a difference between loser = "person who lost" and loser = "worthless failure person". They seem to be going for the first definition, but with a subtle hint at the second, suggesting that your play might lead to you representing a group of crappy superheroes if you don't win the game. Seems fine to me.

It did not seem fine to me for exactly this reason.  Perhaps it's a culture difference; I find it hard to picture Britons calling each other "loser" (if only because you have so many much more cutting insults like "tosser" and "poof", which we Yanks find impossible to take seriously, but which I can objectively tell are pretty vicious to people raised the right way).  But over here, we have always had a strong culture of "winners never quit, quitters never win" and "the measure of a man is the work he does" and so forth (which is a logical extention of being a nation that boostrapped itself into existence in less than 500 years, instead of having millenia of tradition to cling to), so being called any form or variation of "worthless, weak, will never amount to everything" tends to really get to us.  Even a person like me, who actively prides himself on his laziness, can recoil at being judged in such a fashion, particularly when coming from an apparent peer group…such as the gaming community, or "geekdom" in general.  Since most of those I know in sci-fi fandom grew up being 'the uncool people' who were always mistreated by the mainstream, I've come to expect an exquisite level of tolerance and compassion among us, with very few exceptions.  (The trash-talk among Magic gamers being one of those exceptions, but SOTM is not Magic.)

Insulting people isn't a good way to get people to buy games.

Right, which is why I thought it was bad copy.  Why couldn't they say something more charitable?  That said, if "their crowd" responds positively to such a tone, c'est la vie.  I just know damn well that I won't ever buy anything from them if they might call me a Loser before I even click "add to cart".

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
The problem is that associations can be stronger than meanings.  Yes, the ad is using the literal meaning of "loser", and it's easy to recognize what they mean.  But that doesn't prevent the association "Playing SotM = Loser(at life)".  It won't be a strong association, but it will still be there, and it's not an association we want made at all.

 

That being said, if ThinkGeek has a deprecating sense of humor, then that goes a great way to breaking the association.  It's like calling your friend a jerk - you are familiar enough with each other that you know that term is meant in a meaningless fashion, and no negative connotation is attached to the insult.

It also helps that "League of Losers" feels like a reference, even if the readers aren't familiar with it, which also helps break the negative connotations.

 

I do trust ThinkGeek though.  They've had a lot of success selling to the geek community, which is a community with a particularly strong negative association with the term "loser".  It's not something that would slip under the radar.  If it's there, it's because they don't think it's a problem.
